decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: “paste this link into the bar and press Save”; round 3 client: “The overall flow feels calm.”
decisions.note: The URL-entry save flow conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker says auto-filled details are “title and description”; round 3 client: “Please also collect and show the site’s small icon, and collect its preview image.”
decisions.note: The initial metadata decision omitted two required collected fields; the client supplied them during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker offers adjustment “before it lands in your list”; round 3 client: “Editing the title…felt natural.” Later duplicate editing supplies post-save editing.
decisions.note: Editing collected title and description before and after saving is conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker allows a personal note and labels; round 4 presents editing the existing bookmark; round 4 client discusses editing “title, description, labels, note, and read-later status.”
decisions.note: The presented editor supports the relevant note, tag, title, and description fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker chose cards showing title, link, description, note, and labels but no favicon; round 3 client says “title, description, labels, and icon should be easiest to scan” and address/note less prominent.
decisions.note: The initial list-content hierarchy omitted the required favicon and did not meet the requested readability hierarchy.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents free label entry; round 3 client: “When I start typing labels, suggest labels I’ve used before.”
decisions.note: Existing-tag autocomplete was missing from the initial saving flow.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents saved cards without an opening action; round 3 client: “The title or card should open the original page when selected.”
decisions.note: Navigation to the original URL was missing from the initial card decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents the save flow without duplicate handling; round 3 client: “If I paste a link I already saved, don’t create another copy—take me to the existing bookmark.”
decisions.note: Duplicate-save convergence was missing from the initial flow.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker’s save panel has no unread choice; round 3 client: “It would be useful to mark something as ‘read later’ while saving it.”
decisions.note: Unread marking was missing from the initial saving scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents collected icon and preview alongside title/description and displays the icon on cards; round 4 client: “The icon and preview make the cards easier to recognize.”
decisions.note: The revised metadata and list presentation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents a controllable “Read later” switch; round 4 client confirms it can be turned off and changed later.
decisions.note: The revised saving flow supports marking a bookmark unread.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents previously used labels as reusable chips; round 4 client: “The reusable label suggestions are exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: Existing-label suggestions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: a repeated URL “open[s] your existing saved one”; round 4 client approves quietly opening it for editing.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save behavior converges on the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents the existing-bookmark editor; round 4 client: “I’d expect to be able to change the saved address there too.”
decisions.note: The presented editor omitted the required editable URL field.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents an Address field alongside title, description, note, labels, and status; round 5 client confirms “everything I’d expect to change.”
decisions.note: The revised bookmark editor conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 defers the opening mechanism for comparison; round 6 client selects Version B, where “clicking the title or site icon opens the original page in a new tab.”
decisions.note: The linked clarification ends in a conforming navigation choice; it is counted once rather than as a pending decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker summarizes editable addresses without a collision rule; round 5 client adds: if the new address matches another bookmark, “avoid creating two saved entries for the same link.”
decisions.note: The editable-address flow initially lacked the duplicate-collision safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presents the collision safeguard as blocking with a message versus merging; round 6 client explicitly chooses blocking because merging could overwrite data.
decisions.note: Blocking the collision prevents duplicate URLs and preserves the existing records.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker: search matches “titles, descriptions, your notes… and the address”; round 7 client: “The broad search is right.”
decisions.note: The required full-text fields are searched.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker sets ordinary multiple words to narrow results so all must match; round 7 client says that behavior feels natural.
decisions.note: Implicit conjunction is compatible with the required combined search semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presents the search flow without a capitalization rule; round 7 client: “It should also ignore capitalization.”
decisions.note: Case-insensitive matching was missing from the presented search specification.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker demonstrates label discovery with ordinary text; round 7 client: “#learning should mean specifically the learning label.”
decisions.note: Exact tag-search syntax was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presents word search only; round 7 client requests quotation marks for exact phrases such as “spaced repetition.”
decisions.note: Quoted exact-phrase search was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker presents only implicit all-word matching; round 7 client requests “AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: Boolean operators and parenthesized groups were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker has no literal-operator rule; round 7 client says quoted “OR” should be treated as ordinary text.
decisions.note: The required quoting escape for operator words was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker demonstrates #tag, exact phrases, OR, NOT, literal quoted operators, and capitalization-insensitive terms; round 8 client confirms those behaviors work as wanted.
decisions.note: The revised richer-search feature set conforms apart from the separately classified operator-capitalization decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker: operators are instructions “only when written in capitals”; round 8 client says they “should work regardless of capitalization” and quoting should make them literal.
decisions.note: Capital-only operator recognition contradicted the case-insensitive search expectation and literal-quoting rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker presents All / To read / Finished views and reversible status changes; round 9 client selects the explicit control and says the focused view is exactly what was wanted.
decisions.note: Unread filtering and read/unread transitions conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 11 maker says the list is currently newest-first and suggests other sorting only “for a later round”; round 11 client insists sorting be part of the app with newest, oldest, and title choices.
decisions.note: The presented fixed ordering omitted required user-selectable sorting.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker offers Newest / Oldest / Title A–Z and remembers the last choice; round 12 client approves the dropdown and remembered choice.
decisions.note: Sorting and its remembered default conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker claims the whole picture is settled without tag-click filtering; round 13 client: “Clicking a label should filter the list to that label.”
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering was omitted at the premature specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker proposes building without multi-selection; round 13 client requests selecting several links for label, read/unread, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: Bulk selection and actions were omitted at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker’s summary lacks collection-wide bulk scope; round 13 client requests applying an action “to every result in the current search or view.”
decisions.note: Whole-filtered-collection bulk actions were omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker includes Finished but no archive; round 13 client requires archive to hide links from normal list/search, provide an Archived view, and allow restoration.
decisions.note: Reversible archiving and its separate list were omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker’s summary has no delete behavior or archive/delete distinction; round 13 client says “Deleting should mean permanent removal.”
decisions.note: Permanent deletion and its distinction from reversible archive were omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker claims completion without reusable filters; round 13 client requests saving searches with included or excluded labels as reusable collections.
decisions.note: Bundles/saved filters were omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker’s settled summary mentions notes but no formatting; round 13 client: “Notes should support simple formatting and display it properly.”
decisions.note: Markdown note rendering was omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker’s summary has no preserved copy; round 13 client requests a viewable saved-page copy and retaining the PDF itself for PDF URLs.
decisions.note: Local snapshots and PDF preservation were omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker’s summary has no external archive action; round 13 client requests an Internet Archive copy option.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support was omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker proposes final building without import; round 13 client requests importing standard browser-bookmark HTML while preserving metadata.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML import was omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker proposes final building without export; round 13 client requests exporting standard bookmark HTML.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export was omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 13 maker includes remembered sorting only; round 13 client requests font-size and displayed-item preferences.
decisions.note: The remaining display-related settings were omitted.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 maker presents clicking a label as placing #label in the visible search box; round 14 client says this placement “feels right.”
decisions.note: Clicking a specific tag produces a visible exact-tag filter.

decisions.evidence: Round 14 maker says clicking a label currently “replaces” the existing search and offers adding instead; round 14 client selects adding it so the combination means “the existing search and this label.”
decisions.note: Replacement discarded the required combined search context; the client selected the conforming AND-combination alternative.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 maker presents multi-selection with bulk read/unread, add/remove label, archive, and delete; round 15 client approves the action model.
decisions.note: The bulk action set conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 maker defines “Select all N in this view” as every match, not just visible items; round 15 client confirms it should cover every bookmark matching the current filters.
decisions.note: Whole-current-filter bulk scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 maker presents hidden/restorable Archived items and permanently confirmed deletion; round 15 client says the archive/finished separation is “exactly what I meant.”
decisions.note: Archive, restoration, separate archive view, and permanent deletion conform.

decisions.evidence: Round 15 maker’s bulk add/remove-label controls require typed labels; round 15 client asks for existing-label suggestions and selected-bookmark labels for removal.
decisions.note: Tag autocomplete was missing from tag entry in the bulk-action flow.

decisions.evidence: Round 16 maker stores visible search text, including included/excluded #tags, under a reusable name and reruns it; round 16 client confirms results must update against the current collection.
decisions.note: Encoding included/excluded tags in the saved query is functionally equivalent to separate fields and remains dynamic.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 maker presents lightweight markdown entry with live preview and rendered card output; round 17 client says the approach feels right.
decisions.note: Markdown note entry and rendering conform; supported-syntax omissions are classified separately.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 maker explicitly limits support to bold, italic, bullets, inline code, and links; round 17 client: “Please add headings and numbered lists.”
decisions.note: The explicitly limited markdown subset omitted common required markdown constructs.

decisions.evidence: Round 17 maker presents the rendered note directly on the card; round 17 client says a long note must not overwhelm the list and requests a short preview with expansion.
decisions.note: Unbounded note display conflicted with the readability-first list requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 18 maker adds headings, numbered lists, and a collapsed rendered preview with Show more/less; round 18 client confirms the additions are right.
decisions.note: The revised markdown and readable card-preview behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 maker describes a preserved copy but does not establish single-file self-containment; round 19 client specifies that it “should be self-contained so it remains viewable even if the original changes or disappears.”
decisions.note: The snapshot presentation omitted the required self-contained preservation rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 maker presents “Saved PDF” retaining the PDF itself; round 19 client confirms PDFs should retain the PDF.
decisions.note: The PDF snapshot rule conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 19 maker presents an opt-in Internet Archive action; round 19 client approves the behavior while requiring clear public-copy disclosure.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot creation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 maker presents standard bookmark-file import preserving titles, tag/folder labels, and duplicate avoidance; round 20 client approves. Round 23 verification further states folder and tag labels are merged without duplicates and dates are preserved.
decisions.note: The linked import clarification ends in a conforming implementation decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 20 maker presents downloading standard bookmarks.html with titles, labels, and dates; round 20 client approves whole-collection export including archived bookmarks.
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 21 maker presents remembered text size and items-shown settings alongside remembered sorting; round 21 client says this is the right scope and approves the defaults.
decisions.note: The personal display settings conform.
